strengths: Addresses an important and practically relevant gap: evaluates interaction capabilities in search agents, a capability not previously systematized in existing benchmarks like BrowseComp and GAIA
Well-motivated and clever benchmark design using target-distractor methodology that creates genuine ambiguity resolvable only through interaction
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 17 diverse models with thoughtfully designed ablations (answer-only, search-only, with-context) that clearly isolate the interaction bottleneck
Convincing demonstration that failure stems from systematic overconfidence rather than capability deficits, supported by the striking 5× accuracy gap between search-only and with-context settings
Forced interaction experiments (Figure 3b) cleverly reveal latent capability—GPT-5 doubles accuracy when compelled to interact, strengthening the overconfidence diagnosis
Valuable longitudinal analysis showing interaction capabilities stagnated over 15 months while search performance improved 7-fold, identifying a critical blind spot in agent development
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-documented implementation details supporting reproducibility
Bilingual dataset (English and Chinese) enables cross-linguistic evaluation
weaknesses: Dataset size (210 questions across 9 domains) is modest for a benchmark; no justification provided and no comparison to related benchmarks. Some domains are underrepresented (Medicine & Life Science 5.7%, Academic & Research 4.7%)

Quality assurance metrics lack transparency: no quantitative data on verification outcomes (rejection/revision rates), inter-annotator agreement not reported, and no discussion of how disagreements were resolved

Simulated responder validity not established: GPT-4o (temperature=1.0) introduces unexplored randomness, lacks comparison to human behavior, and 3-trial validation (k=3) is insufficient. No ablation on temperature or model choice
Automated grading using GPT-4o introduces unknown error rates; vague 'spot-checking against human evaluation' without reporting agreement rates or failure modes
Agent evaluation limited to ReAct framework with heavily prompt-engineered system prompts (Appendix A.1); sensitivity to prompt variations unexplored and generalization unclear

Incomplete analysis: forced interaction shows model-specific divergent responses without investigation of why (e.g., why does Claude-Sonnet-4 not benefit while GPT-5 doubles?), scaling analysis limited to 50 questions, no error analysis by question type/domain
No qualitative investigation of interaction strategies or error modes; missing per-domain performance breakdown and question difficulty analysis
Statistical reporting inconsistent: standard deviations reported irregularly, no significance testing between models, calibration error metric (5 bins) is coarse
Algorithm 1 lacks formal specification with unspecified loop termination conditions; annotation instructions are open-ended without detailed guidelines shown

Missing critical baselines: no human performance evaluation, no direct empirical comparison with related interaction benchmarks (IN3, Tau-Bench), and limited generalization discussion for target-distractor ambiguity applicability

Longitudinal analysis sparse and potentially unfair: comparing 7-fold BrowseComp improvement to flat InteractComp ignores that different task types may have different improvement curves; no analysis of model lineage progression
Limited discussion of limitations: insufficient treatment of potential negative applications, ethical considerations, and how results generalize beyond search domain

strengths: Well-motivated benchmark addressing genuine gap: existing search benchmarks assume complete queries, missing the practical failure mode of ambiguous information needs
Thoughtful target-distractor methodology ensuring controlled, verifiable ambiguity that requires interaction to resolve
Rigorous two-stage verification with cross-paraphrasing, manual Google checks, and automated validation using multiple capable models
Comprehensive evaluation across 17 diverse models with four complementary configurations (Answer-only, Answer+Search, Answer+Interact, Answer+Search+Interact) that systematically isolate capabilities

Striking empirical findings: 5× performance gap (13.73% vs 71.50%) demonstrating systematic overconfidence; forced interaction doubling accuracy (14%→40%) proves latent capability; longitudinal stagnation in interaction vs 7-fold search improvement over 15 months

Strong robustness validation: human responder agreement (α=0.707), responder sensitivity analysis, commercial system evaluation (OpenAI/Doubao Deep Research similarly fail), ranking consistency tests, and interaction utility analysis distinguishing quality from quantity
Clear, well-structured presentation with compelling visualizations (Figure 1) and comprehensive implementation details enabling reproducibility; code promised to be available

Valuable diagnostic insights: error attribution distinguishing strategic failures (overconfidence: 1-70%) from tactical failures (identification errors: 17-88%), and natural language interaction experiments showing increased bandwidth doesn't solve core problem
weaknesses: Modest dataset size (210 instances) compared to contemporary benchmarks; while HumanEval precedent is cited, scale limits generalizability and downstream training applications
Limited domain scope: 9 domains without per-domain analysis; unclear whether findings generalize equally. Absence of domain breakdown leaves questions about systematic difficulties

Artificial task construction via target-distractor methodology may not reflect naturally occurring ambiguity patterns; questions forced to 1-2 word answers limiting scope to factoid retrieval; no evidence of transfer to natural ambiguous queries
Missing human baseline: no human performance provided for calibration, making it unclear whether 13.73% accuracy is appropriately difficult or artificially constrained

Incomplete investigation of core findings: (1) 'systematic' overconfidence claimed but primarily supported by performance gap; deeper confidence distribution analysis needed; (2) forced interaction reaches only 40% vs 67.88% ceiling—27.88% gap unexplained; (3) error categories coarse (4 types); tactical vs strategic failures need finer granularity

Simulated responder limitations: GPT-4o bias concerns unexamined; human agreement α=0.707 acceptable but suboptimal for repeated training use; temperature settings differ (responder 1.0 vs agents 0.6) with fairness implications unaddressed
Statistical rigor gaps: no significance testing despite overlapping confidence intervals (e.g., GPT-5 13.73%±2.55); Kendall's τ reported for ranking but no within-condition hypothesis tests

Search implementation constraints: restricted to top-5 results without sensitivity analysis; Google Serper API dependency limits reproducibility; search as potential bottleneck under-explored relative to interaction

Model analysis gaps: stark open-weight vs proprietary divide (13.08% vs 13.73%) not investigated; unclear if inherent capability or training objective differences; insufficient exploration of why similar models show different interaction patterns

Missing comparative analysis: no direct numerical comparison with related interaction benchmarks (UserBench, IN3, Tau-Bench); no naturally occurring ambiguous query comparison; no cross-domain performance breakdown despite variable domain sizes (Science 21.3% vs Sports 7.1%)

strengths: Well-motivated problem identifying a genuine gap in search agent evaluation: most benchmarks assume complete queries while real-world users have ambiguous needs requiring clarification

Rigorous benchmark construction using elegant target-distractor methodology that ensures genuine ambiguity unresolvable through search alone, with thorough two-stage verification including cross-paraphrasing

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation: 17 diverse models, systematic ablations (answer-only, search-only, ask-only, with-context), scaling analysis (5/10/20 rounds), forced interaction, natural language interaction variants, error attribution analysis, and extensive robustness checks

Clear diagnostic findings strongly supported by evidence: systematic overconfidence (70% of GPT-5 failures vs 17% identification errors) is primary bottleneck, not reasoning deficits; forced interaction doubles accuracy, proving latent capability exists
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, complete system prompts, experimental configurations (Table A2), promised code release, and thorough appendices with robustness analyses
Clean verifiable reward signals from search outcomes make benchmark ideal substrate for future RL-based training approaches like RLVR
Strong presentation: well-structured, clearly motivated, effective visualizations (especially Figure 1 showing performance gap), appropriate caveats and limitations discussion
Bilingual dataset (66% English, 34% Chinese) enables cross-linguistic evaluation, increasing generality
weaknesses: Modest dataset size (210 questions) raises concerns about statistical stability (e.g., GPT-5: ±2.55% standard deviation) and generalization, particularly compared to recent benchmarks with 289+ instances; no significance testing provided

Simulated responder using GPT-4o introduces potential biases; human validation shows only moderate agreement (κ=0.756-0.693, α=0.707); matched responder experiments show notable variations (e.g., Gemini: 10%→6%); no analysis of responder error propagation effects

Binary yes/no interaction protocol is artificially constrained compared to real clarification (which typically allows follow-ups, conditionals, quantitative responses); natural language experiments show gap persists (GPT-5: 25.71% vs 67.88%), leaving unclear whether protocol restrictions vs fundamental limitations explain performance

Limited scope of ambiguity types: focuses solely on factoid QA where target is confused with similar distractor; doesn't capture underspecified goals, context-dependent interpretations, preference ambiguity, or open-ended information needs; generalization to other query types unclear

Insufficient analysis of effective interaction strategies: shows asking more questions doesn't help (Table B3) but provides limited guidance on what makes good clarification; error categories are coarse (17-88% identification, 1-70% overconfidence); no analysis of hardest-to-discover attributes or question ordering effects

Longitudinal analysis limitations: compares different models across time points rather than evolution of single model, making it unclear whether stagnation reflects fundamental limits or model development priorities; no analysis of *why* interaction improvements plateaued
Fixed 10-round interaction budget potentially arbitrary; scaling analysis only on 50-question subset; unclear how results generalize to queries genuinely requiring 50+ clarifications

Missing mechanistic insights: limited explanation for why overconfidence emerges, why different models show different failure modes (GPT-5: 70% overconfidence vs Claude: 88% identification), or how forced interaction actually improves performance
Calibration error improvements through interaction might reflect forced uncertainty rather than genuine capability gains; with-context ceiling may be noisy with model-dependent failure modes
No real user study validation of simulated responder on non-trivial subset; no statistical significance testing for reported differences
